result.document_summary: Part 4 of 4 of the NJ Department of Community Affairs Truth in Renting guide, covering remaining just-cause eviction grounds, owner-occupied 2-3 family evictions, rooming houses, penalties, reprisal, foreclosure tenant protections, and agency contact lists.
result.notes: Part 4 continues the NJ Anti-Eviction Act (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1) discussion with grounds (m) through (r), plus the owner-occupied two- and three-family regime under 2A:18-61.2. These are recorded as one state just-cause eviction instrument. The Truth in Renting guide gives no effective dates in this part. The foreclosure tenant notice rules are not treated as a separate in-scope category beyond the eviction regime. Contact lists and procedural court details were ignored as out of scope.

rules.title: NJ Anti-Eviction Act: additional good-cause grounds (employment termination, drug, assault, theft, human trafficking offenses) and owner-occupied 2-3 family regime
rules.requirement: A landlord may evict only for statutory good causes, including termination of a superintendent's employment, drug offenses, assault or terroristic threats, theft, and human trafficking, generally after a three-day Notice to Quit and within two years of the conviction or release. Tenants of owner-occupied two- and three-family dwellings may be removed only by court order on enumerated causes, with 1-month or 3-month notices where applicable.
rules.key_value: 3-day Notice to Quit; 2-year filing limit for offense-based grounds
rules.quoted_span: Tenants of landlord-occupied two- and three-family dwellings can be removed only when a court issues an order for eviction.
rules.coverage_text: Residential rental tenancies in New Jersey subject to the Anti-Eviction Act; owner-occupied two- and three-family dwellings are covered by a separate, narrower set of causes.
rules.interaction: Public housing authorities must follow these State eviction laws as well as HUD regulations (24 C.F.R. 966); rooming and boarding houses must follow the same good-cause and notice requirements unless the Bureau orders otherwise.
